title: Customer Brickstack: annotated threads + prioritized probe plan
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, annotated roll-up of customer threads we collected across May–June 2028 (support tickets, field interviews, and partner calls). The goal is to surface high-impact runtime frictions and a small set of prioritized probes we can run in the next 6 weeks. This is intentionally pragmatic: 3 near-term probes (sprint-friendly), 2 medium-term platform asks for Eng+Product alignment, and a handful of illustrative customer quotes that clarify the pain.

How this was assembled:
- Sources: 32 support tickets tagged 'latency', 14 partner calls, 6 solution-engineering field notes, and automated VOC capture from the console feedback widget (top 200 impressions).
- Signal weighting: frequency (40%), severity (30%), revenue-exposure (20%), implementation effort (10%).
- Quick filters applied: only items tied to inference latency/cost, model routing, KV cache behaviors, and rollout/backoff UX.

Raw customer vignettes (edited):
- "Sometimes responses stall at 300 tokens — we see 1.2s spikes that break our streaming UX." — fintech prod lead, $1.2M ARR
- "When we switched to a quantized variant, hallucination rate jumped; we'd like a traffic-split mechanism to test quality in prod." — marketplace startup
- "Cache invalidation on user edits confuses us; prefix caching seems opaque and leads to stale completions." — healthcare partner (private deploy)
- "Dedicated pool cold-starts are killing us during nightly batch inference windows." — edtech company

Top themes (synthesized):
1) Observability blind spots around per-request routing and model-variant fallbacks. Customers can see tokens and latency but cannot reliably map a request to the exact model variant + kernel selection that served it.
2) KV/prefix cache semantics and visibility. Operators want an explicit cache dashboard (hits/misses per-prefix, TTLs, and invalidation traces). They also want safe invalidation primitives for content edits.
3) Quality-regression testing in production. Teams need an easy way to split traffic between model variants (quantized vs float) and capture eval metrics on a held prompt set before rolling out.
4) Cold-start and burst handling for Dedicated (predictable throughput vs cost). Requests during bursts either queue unpredictably or fallback to lower-capacity models with little explanation.
5) UX/Docs gaps for retry/backoff behavior and how batching affects tail latency.

Prioritized probes (next 6 weeks) — quick wins and owners:
A. Cache Inspector Spike (2 sprints) — deliverable: lightweight console view + API endpoint returning per-prefix hit/miss and last-invalidated timestamp. Owner: Omar (CS) + Eng-Observability (Diego to lead). Success signal: 75% of pilot customers can correlate a stale output to a cache miss within 5 minutes. Risk: data volume; start with per-customer sampled telemetry.

B. Traffic-Split Canary for Variant Quality (3 sprints) — deliverable: UI flow and API for 0-10% traffic splits, automatic eval capture against a stored prompt set, and side-by-side quality diffs (BLEU/ROUGE + small human labeling tag). Owner: Product-Hosted-API (Lena) + Research. Success signal: customers can detect quality regressions in <48h on a 1% split. Risk: metric reliability; start with deterministic prompt sets.

C. Cold-Start Observability + Warmup Hook (2 sprints) — deliverable: trace spans that mark cold vs warm model instances and a config hook to run a warmup prompt on node start. Owner: Eng-Infra (SRE liaison: Sophie). Success signal: measured 30% reduction in tail latency during scheduled bursts for pilot customers. Risk: warmup cost; make warmups optional per-pool.

Medium-term platform asks (quarter-level):
1) Per-request model variant metadata in logs (model id, quantization profile, kernel selection). This is an engineering lift (schema + storage) but eliminates a large class of debugging cycles. Suggested PM: Product-Hosting.
2) Accessible, productized cache invalidation primitives (prefix-scoped tombstones, TTL override APIs) with audit logs. High-value for Private deployments and Dedicated customers. Suggested PM: Private.

Quick prioritization rationale:
- Cache Inspector + Traffic-Split Canary are prioritized because they unblock multiple customer asks (stale outputs, quality regression, safe experiments) and can be delivered incrementally with sampling to limit storage and cost.
- Cold-start warmup is prioritized because an operational tweak can materially reduce customer SLA incidents and is relatively contained in scope.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Telemetry ingestion: start with sampled 5% telemetry for Cache Inspector to avoid early scale issues. Tag telemetry by customer-id and pool-id.
- Data retention: store sampled traces for 30 days for debugging; longer retention can be an opt-in add-on.
- Privacy: for healthcare customers on Private, strip PII from telemetry and add KMS tagging in the pipeline.

Success metrics (proposal):
- Reduction in 'stale completion' incidents reported by pilot customers by 60% within 8 weeks of Cache Inspector rollout.
- Ability to detect quality regressions (precision/recall of flagged regressions) at >80% on controlled prompt sets for Traffic-Split Canary.
- 25% reduction in cold-start related SLO breaches for Dedicated pools in pilot accounts.

Open questions and decisions required:
- Sampling policy: Who has permission to opt-in/opt-out customers from telemetry sampling? (ops vs customer).
- Metric definitions: Which quality metrics matter for non-NLP outputs (semantic similarity vs token overlap)? Need Research input.
- Rollout policy: Can we wire automatic fallback to float variants if a canary shows regression, or do we only surface the signal to customers?

Suggested next steps (this week):
- Align on Probe A scope at Monday sync; decide data schema for Cache Inspector (owner: Omar).
- Product/Research pair to scope the minimum eval set for Traffic-Split Canary (owner: Lena).
- SRE to prototype a warmup hook and cost model (owner: Sophie).
- CS to recruit 4 pilot customers for early trials (Maya to coordinate).

Meeting prep notes for pilot kickoff:
- Ask pilots to provide: 1) 10 canonical prompts that capture their core latency/quality expectations; 2) traffic windows for burst simulation; 3) contact for private telemetry.
- Share an opt-in telemetry agreement and an explainer doc on what data is collected and how it will be used.

Appendix — shorthand backlog (for planning):
- Small: add model-variant id to request logs (low-impact logging change).
- Medium: API for prefix tombstone invalidation (requires audit trail).
- Medium: console UX for traffic-split toggles and historical comparison charts.
- Large: rollout policies with automated rollback based on eval metrics.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider a 'sample and re-score' job that takes 1% traffic and runs a heavier evaluator offline to reduce real-time metric noise.
- In Private deployments, expose a localized cache inspector UI that queries the customer-managed control plane to avoid cross-tenant telemetry flow.

Decision log stub:
- 2028-06-21: Document created to consolidate field signal.
- 2028-06-25: Team agreed to pilot Cache Inspector with 4 customers; Omar to draft data schema.

End of roll-up.

-- Maya (CS) — questions/comments: add to this doc or ping in slack #cs-field-threads.
